title: Lambdas as text strategies

blocks.text: A strategy interface with one method is a functional interface, so a lambda or a method reference can be the strategy, and `UnaryOperator<String>` is already the interface a text strategy needs. The page also keeps stateless strategies as `static final` constants.

items: The constructor and `setStrategy(s)` keep the strategy and refuse `null` with `IllegalArgumentException`.
`process(text)` returns the strategy applied to `text`; **`null` text is refused** with `IllegalArgumentException` before the strategy runs.

Five constants: `UPPER_CASE`, `LOWER_CASE`, `REVERSE`, `TRIM_AND_UPPER` and `REMOVE_WHITESPACE`. **Case changes use `Locale.ROOT`**, so they give the same answer on every machine. **`REMOVE_WHITESPACE` removes every whitespace character** (spaces, tabs, newlines).

cases.says: process() applies the held strategy; the five constants do what their names say; setStrategy() accepts any lambda.
REMOVE_WHITESPACE removes tabs, newlines and runs of spaces, not only single spaces.
With a Turkish default locale, UPPER_CASE still turns "title" into "TITLE" and LOWER_CASE turns "TITLE" into "title".
process(null) throws IllegalArgumentException instead of handing null to the strategy.
Both the constructor and setStrategy() refuse null with IllegalArgumentException.

concepts: A single-method strategy is a functional interface, so lambdas, method references and standard types like UnaryOperator can be strategies, kept as static final constants when stateless.
